posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Looking through everything added in this thread since update #3... it still seems a little lacking, story-wise.

 

Bowman III has been an archer/athlete all his life.  He used to be the leader of a teen hero group, now he's in the Freedom League.  But there's literally nothing else to him.  (Incidentally, the whole Kickstarter update can be found on the Obsidian Portal character sheet and bio, so we can persumably read up on all the other heroes there as well.)  However, we do get an idea of his mechanics from the Atomic Think Tank page, basically, gimmick arrows a la the comic book Green Arrow or the MCU Hawkeye.

Captain Thunder is apparently a statesman, despite being "Captain Thunder" full time, and a "family hero" similar to Legacy.  I'm satisfied with the amount of background put into him.  Mechanics will be tough, though.

Daedalus actually has a really thorough story.  No complaints there at all.  Mechanically, in addition to protection and strength, the suit comes with gravity-controlling powers and vision enhancements that let him see things on the atomic level and see through solid objects.  Gold standard stuff here.

Dr. Metropolis is also all mechanics and no background/personality, he just sort of showed up one day and does what he does.  The Atomic Think Tank character sheet even goes so far as to have him be severely weakened and eventually die outside a city. He's going to be a serious design challenge.  Good luck Christopher!

Johnny Rocket: Another career superhero with no background or personality besides "fast" and the fact that he's gay.  Yawn.  He does seem to have some abilities centered around creating wind flow (e.g. tornadoes) with his speed, which will be a nice hook for Christopher.

Lady Liberty: Was in pre-law.  Other than being very patriotic, that's pretty much all there is to know about her as a person.  Power-wise, though, she has some potential: in addition to the usual flight and strength, she has healing powers and apparently some firework/explosion stuff.  I guess she's probably the one Christopher mentioned in the podcast as having a shield that isn't documented anywhere.

Pseudo has a pretty thorough background, too.  Good stuff on the Atomic page.  Christopher will have both some espionage (mind-reading and becoming insubstanial) and shapechanging abilities to work with.

Siren is basically like Ra.  Lots to work with here.

Star Knight: A former cop.  Backstory is essentially a cross between the Green Lantern and agent J from Men in Black.  I don't have a good feel for her abilities other than armor, flight, and an energy sword.

The Raven: Yet another career superhero with not much else in the way of background.  She's basically the daughter of Batman, trained to be just like him.  Making her different from Wraith is going to be a serious design challenge.

 

So to sum up, we have 5 heroes who are plain-vanilla and have not much background or life outside of being a superhero, two or three that are OK, and two or three that are pretty good.  Mechanically, we have four or five that will be tough to make interesting, four or five that have some clear potential, and one that will undoubtedly be interesting but will be hard to reconcile with the lore in a way that makes sense and is fun.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
My assessment of the situation:
 
I agree that the main audience for this is most likely people who like M&M or have heard of it. Green Ronin is a well-established company that's been around for some time, and puts out one of the iconic and well-known systems in the tabletop RPG fandom. They probably figured their main goal was to sell the Sentinels game mechanics to people already familiar with the M&M content, not the other way around.
 
On top of that, I'm betting they made what turned out to be an incorrect assumption about the Sentinels fandom. They probably assumed that we really loved the card game mechanics, and so it would be easy to sell us on more decks to play with our mechanics. They probably didn't realize how much the Sentinels fandom cares deeply about the flavor of the game as well, so didn't realize they'd need to pimp their own flavor so strongly right away.
 
Which is to be expected that they came from a different way of thinking when you are an RPG company where your system is the main thrust of your product and while you come up with fluff it's assumed your players are going to mostly come up with their own fluff and only dip into yours here and there and piecemeal as they need it for their own thing.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Jeysie:

I think we're pretty spoiled by writing as SotM fans. Basically Christopher is like Al Ewing in a world full of Bendis.

 

I find this sentence to be very humourous, because as SotM fans, writing is the one thing we have the least of.

 

Seriously.  All of the story related text that we have fits on the Wiki.  All of it.

 

Christopher and Adam's stories are good, but I don't think that the stories are particularly amazing.  Their true genius is in the way they've managed to convey those stories using a bare minimum of art, text, and rules.  The delivery, rather than the content.

 

The level of story integration that SotM achieves will be difficult for SoEP because of the seperation between the design team (GtG) and the creative team (Green Ronin), but I am not particualrly worried.

 

There is, however, a danger of a self-fulfilling prophecy.  This type of storytelling relies heavily on allowing the readers/players to fill in the gaps with their previous knowledge of comic book and general story tropes, and general imagination.  If prejudice against the story causes people to refuse to fill the gaps that they filled while playing SotM, then they will find themselves dissatisfied with SoEP for completely avoidable reasons without ever noticing why.
